findings.summary: Call completion can overwrite a concurrent stop. _finish_goal_call_owned reads the current mode and computes next_mode before append_many, without synchronization with stop. If completion reads running, then a graceful stop records stopping while the call remains in flight, completion subsequently persists its stale running/waiting mode and releases the fence. Queued requests can then start without resume, and reconstruction retains the overwritten mode. A confirmed immediate stop can be overwritten through the same interleaving. The new completion-recovery tests cover missing mode records and sequential drainage, not concurrent control transitions. Serialize completion's mode derivation, persistence, projection update and fence release with stop/resume and call admission; add a barrier-controlled offline regression proving a stop cannot be lost. This violates behavior 5 and P6 without requiring live Runtime testing.

Continuous independently records APPROVE for implementation subject 8545dc97e11a02aca24681d7a78c0672391e27ac. Final independently records REJECT for the concurrent lifecycle defect above. Those fixes do not establish atomicity against concurrent stop.
